name: Retentive Network: A Successor to Transformer for Large Language Models
problem: Transformers need attention to model token interactions; recurrent models cannot parallelise training. The choice of sequence-mixing primitive forces that trade-off, and no prior alternative offered training parallelism, O(1) inference and Transformer-level quality at once.
mechanism: Retention: a sequence-mixing primitive derived by a theoretical link between recurrence and attention, expressed in THREE equivalent paradigms - parallel (for training), recurrent (for O(1) inference), and chunkwise recurrent (for long sequences: encode each chunk in parallel while recurrently summarising the chunks). All three are the same function, so one set of weights serves training and serving without conversion.
speedup_reported: The abstract makes NO numeric speedup claim: it reports 'favourable scaling results, parallel training, low-cost deployment, and efficient inference'. The O(1) inference and improved decoding throughput/latency/GPU-memory claims are structural consequences of the recurrent form, stated without a multiplier or a baseline engine. Anything quantified here would be invented.
notes: arXiv ID 2307.08621 verified via abs-page citation_title/citation_date on 2026-10-03; title matches. VENUE: recorded as arxiv-preprint on EVIDENCE, which differs from the common citation. So the three-paradigm idea is genuinely research-only.
